QASHANI:90:8-14/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:90:8-14/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:90:8-14/r1.claim: Bodily faculties enable people to gain perfection, see lessons, ask about what they do not know, and speak; God directs them to good and evil paths.
QASHANI:90:8-14/r1.anchor: الآلات البدنية التي يتمكن بها من اكتساب الكمال ليبصر ما يعتبر به

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p317/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p317/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p317/r5.claim: Verses 8–17 list eyes, speech, moral awareness, freeing slaves, feeding the poor, faith, patience, and compassion as capacities and deeds that should overcome greed and serve God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p317/r5.anchor: the Almighty had given them eyes so that they could use them to learn the lessons of life, tongue and lips so that they could use them to urge people in helping the poor

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p323/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p323/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p323/r1.claim: Wealth has so distracted the addressees that they have not properly used their eyes to notice the needy around them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p324/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p324/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p324/r1.claim: Exhortation is included in the believer’s obligation; without it, the virtuous deed remains incomplete.

JISHUMI:v10p7416/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7416/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7416/r6.claim: One coherence reading asks how a person can think God does not see him when God created him and gave him eyes, a tongue, and lips.
JISHUMI:v10p7416/r6.anchor: كيف يحسب أن لا يراه الله وهو الذي خلقه، وجعل له عينين

JISHUMI:v10p7416/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7416/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7416/r7.claim: A second reading connects the gifts of the senses to the hardship of moral responsibility: God removed the person's excuse by giving him these faculties.
JISHUMI:v10p7416/r7.anchor: أنه يتصل بقوله: (لقد خلقنا الإنسان في كبد) حيث كلفناه، ولكن أزحنا علته

JISHUMI:v10p7416/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7416/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7416/r8.claim: A third reading answers the claim that no one can overpower a person: God created his eyes, tongue, and lips; the eyes see proofs and the tongue and lips speak.
JISHUMI:v10p7416/r8.anchor: أنه يتصل بقوله: (أن لن يقدر عليه أحد) كيف ظن ذلك وقد خلقناه

JISHUMI:v10p7416/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7416/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7416/r9.claim: A fourth reading uses the body's wondrous capacities as evidence against the unbeliever and says God guided him, so his unbelief is his own doing.
JISHUMI:v10p7416/r9.anchor: وبدأ بالعين لعجيب خلقته في الرؤية، وباللسان لعجيب خلقته في الكلام

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r1.claim: The passage shifts from rhetorical questions to categorical judgment: a human endowed with insight and choice fails the moral standard, failing to take the steep path.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:11-16:kommentar/r1.anchor: Mit Beginn des dritten Gesätzes – das sich immer noch pronominal auf den in V. 90:4 eingeführten ʾinsān zurückbezieht – schlägt das zuvor von rhetorischen Fragen geprägte Register des Textes in einen kategorischen Tonfall um

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r1.claim: The surah's hardships call for patience: choosing either path, climbing the ascent, serving the enslaved, enduring famine, and caring for orphans and the destitute all demand perseverance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p274/r1.anchor: وسلوك النجدين يحتاج إلى صبر لما في صعودهما وسلوكهما من تعب ونَصَب، واقتحام العقبة يحتاج إلى صبر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p276/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p276/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p276/r1.claim: Patience comes first because the surah has already described human toil, the difficult ascent, and the two paths; mercy follows the subsequent duties of freeing and feeding.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p276/r1.anchor: فقدم التواصي بالصبر لمّا تقدّم ما يدعو إليه

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r1.claim: The senses gather knowledge from the external world, while the “two paths” generally mean good and evil and represent the ability to judge true or false, good or bad, and choose.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r1.anchor: Duyu organları dış dünyadan bilgi edinme araçlarıdır; “iki yol” ise genellikle “iyilik ve kötülük yolları” olarak açıklanmış olup

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r2.claim: In brief, God endowed humans with knowledge, thought, judgment, and choice, making them exceptional and responsible beings.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:90:8/r2.anchor: Allah Teâlâ’nın insana bilgi edinme, düşünüp yargıda bulunma ve seçim yapma yetenekleri lutfederek bu yetenekleriyle onu yeryüzünün en seçkin varlığı halinde yarattığı anlatılmaktadır

BURSEVI:v10p336#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p336#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p336#3/r8.claim: The eyes let a person see the visible world from earth to heaven, distinguish benefit from harm, and view the world, Qur'an, and signs of God.
BURSEVI:v10p336#3/r8.anchor: يبصر بهما عالم الملك من الأرض إلى السماء حتى يشاهد بهما في طرفة عين

BURSEVI:v10p337/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p337/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p337/r1.claim: The eye is a bright mirror that receives images; its small pupil, rapid movement, lids, and lashes protect sight and keep out flies and vermin.
BURSEVI:v10p337/r1.anchor: نحرس ابدن من الآفات وهي نيرة كالمرءآة إذ قابلها شيء ارتسمت صورته فيها

BURSEVI:v10p337/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p337/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p337/r2.claim: Eyes sit in the head like a lamp on a beacon and come as a pair like sun and moon; dark brows and pupils reduce glare, while black lashes strengthen sight.
BURSEVI:v10p337/r2.anchor: وجعلها ثنتين كالشمس والقمر فإنهما عينا التعين الدنيوي

BURSEVI:v10p337/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p337/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p337/r3.claim: The account links black clothing to looking at white marble, whose brightness weakens sight, and says antimony strengthens vision.
BURSEVI:v10p337/r3.anchor: ولذا قال عليه السلام في الأثمد إنه يقوي البصر وجعل الحدقة محركة

BURSEVI:v10p337/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p337/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p337/r4.claim: The movable pupil sees in different directions without turning the neck, and the two eyes share one level so a single object is not seen twice.
BURSEVI:v10p337/r4.anchor: وجعل النظارين جميعا على خط مستقيم عرضا ولم يقع واحد منهما أعلى

BURSEVI:v10p337/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p337/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p337/r5.claim: The pair of eyes also signals an outer and an inner eye, both of which should be guarded because binocular sight is more complete.
BURSEVI:v10p337/r5.anchor: وفي العينين إشارة إلى العين الظاهرة والعين الباطنة فينبغي أن يحافظ على كلتيهما

SULAMI:v2p395#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p395#3/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p395#3/r1.claim: The bodily eye sees signs of divine workmanship, while the heart's eye sees the loci of the unseen.
SULAMI:v2p395#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : عينا في رأسه يصبر بها آثار الصنع

SULAMI:v2p395#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p395#3/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p395#3/r2.claim: One eye perceives created things; the special eye in the special inner locus perceives the Creator.
SULAMI:v2p395#3/r2.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : عينا يرى بها الأكوان وعينا خاصا

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434#2/r1.claim: Qatada says the two eyes are recurring blessings from God, reminders that people should give thanks.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3434#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة الم نجعل له عينين قال : نعم من الله متظاهرة يقررنا بها كيما نشكر

IBNASHUR:90:8/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:8/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:90:8/r1.claim: The question explains the rebuke of people who think no one can overpower or see them: God created perception and speech, so the giver of knowledge cannot be powerless or ignorant.
IBNASHUR:90:8/r1.anchor: أي هو غافل عن قدرة الله تعالى وعن علمه المحيط بجميع الكائنات الدال عليهما أنه خَلَق مشاعر الإِدراك

IBNASHUR:90:8/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:8/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:90:8/r2.claim: The question may be confirmatory or reproachful.
IBNASHUR:90:8/r2.anchor: والاستفهام يجوز أن يكون تقريرياً وأن يكون إنكارياً

IBNASHUR:90:8/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:90:8/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:90:8/r3.claim: Eyes are singled out because they are the most useful sense and because the immediate point challenges the assumption that no one sees the person.
IBNASHUR:90:8/r3.anchor: والاقتصار على العينين لأنهما أنفع المشاعر ولأن المعلَّل إنكار ظنه إن لم يره أحد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r6.claim: The next verses explain the rebuke: the creator of human perception and speech must know and be able to judge people's acts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r6.anchor: فكيف يكون مفيض العلم على الناس غير قادر وغير عالم بأحوالهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r7.claim: The rhetorical question may seek assent or reject the boast; eyes are singled out as the most useful senses and directly answer his claim that nobody saw him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p353/r7.anchor: والاقتصار على العينين لأنهما أنفع المشاعر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p354/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p354/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p354/r1.claim: The progression completes the foundations of learning: senses acquire knowledge, speech communicates it, and guidance helps distinguish and test good and evil.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p132/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p132/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p132/r1.claim: Giving him two eyes is one of the signs that God can resurrect him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p132/r1.anchor: والمعنى ألم نفعل به ما يدل على أن الله قادر على بعثه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r1.claim: The eyes see, the tongue expresses inner thoughts, and the lips help with speech, eating, drinking, and blowing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p759/r1.anchor: يبصر بهما المرئيات { ولسانا } يترجم به عن ضمائره

NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p340#6/r1.claim: God gave him two eyes with which to see visible things.

QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r14.claim: God knows and can reckon his conduct; the eyes, tongue, and lips recall divine favor and God’s ability to resurrect and account for deeds.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r14.anchor: ألم يعلم أن الله قادر على محاسبته، وأن الله عز وجل يرى صنيعه، ثم عدد عليه نعمه

QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r15.claim: The eyes enable sight, the tongue speech, and the lips cover the mouth.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r15.anchor: يبصر بهما { ولسانا } ينطق به. { وشفتين } يستر بهما ثغره

QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r16.speaker: أبو حازم
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r16.claim: Abu Hazim attributes a Prophetic report that God gave lips, eyelids, and protective coverings to restrain forbidden speech, sight, and desire.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9/r16.anchor: قال أبو حازم: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9#2/r7.claim: Qatada says the visible favors remind people so they will be grateful.
QURTUBI-FULL:90:5-9#2/r7.anchor: وقال قتادة: نعم الله ظاهرة، يقررك بها حتى تشكر

QUTB-ZILAL:90:8/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:90:8/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:90:8/r1.claim: The eyes' precise construction and sight are gifts that guide a person through the sensible world, yet the recipient boasts and withholds what God provided.
QUTB-ZILAL:90:8/r1.anchor: جعل له عينين على هذا القدر من الدقة في تركيبهما وفي قدرتهما على الإبصار

RAZI-FULL:v31p166#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#3/r3.claim: The segment gives only the verse text about eyes, tongue, lips, and the two paths, without commentary on those verses.
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#3/r3.anchor: ألم نجعل له عينين * ولسانا وشفتين * وهديناه النجدين

RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r1.claim: The created eyes, tongue, lips, and guidance to two paths demonstrate God's power against the disbeliever's claim that no one can overpower him.
RAZI-FULL:v31p166#4/r1.anchor: ألم نجعل له عينين * ولسانا وشفتين * وهديناه النجدين

STUDYQURAN:90:8/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:90:8/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:90:8/r1.claim: The One capable of making subtle, beneficial instruments such as eyes, tongue, and lips can know every deed and hold people accountable for their use.
STUDYQURAN:90:8/r1.anchor: one who is able to make these subtle instruments from which human beings derive great benefit would certainly be able to know every deed

TAB:90:8/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:90:8/r1.speaker: author
TAB:90:8/r1.claim: God gave the person two eyes to see His proofs, a tongue to express what he wants, and lips as a blessing.
TAB:90:8/r1.anchor: ألم نجعل لهذا القائل أهْلَكْتُ مالاً لُبَدا عينين يبصر بهما حُجَج الله عليه ،   ولسانا يعبر به عن نفسه

TAB:90:8/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:90:8/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB:90:8/r2.claim: Qatāda calls the eyes, tongue, and lips manifest blessings by which God reminds people to be grateful.
TAB:90:8/r2.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  أَلَمْ نَجْعَلْ لَهُ عَيْنَيْنِ وَلِسانا وَشَفَتَيْنِ نِعَم من الله متظاهرة

TABRISI:90:20#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:90:20#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:90:20#2/r3.claim: The created eyes connect with the previous claim: how can someone think God does not see him after receiving eyes?
TABRISI:90:20#2/r3.anchor: كيف يحسب هذا الإنسان أن الله سبحانه لا يراه وهو الذي خلقه وجعل له عينين

TABRISI:90:20#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:90:20#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:90:20#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, the eyes follow the account of human hardship: God tested humanity with commands and removed its excuse by giving it eyes.
TABRISI:90:20#2/r4.anchor: أي اختبرناه حيث كلفناه ثم أزحنا علته بأن جعلنا له عينين

TABRISI:90:20#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:90:20#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:90:20#2/r5.claim: A further connection rebuts the claim that nobody can overpower the person: God made the organs by which he sees proofs and speaks.
TABRISI:90:20#2/r5.anchor: والمعنى كيف يظن ذلك وقد خلقناه وخلقنا أعضاءه

THALABI:v10p208/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p208/r9.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v10p208/r9.claim: Qatāda says the two eyes, tongue, and lips are conspicuous gifts given so that a person will be compelled to thank God.
THALABI:v10p208/r9.anchor: قال قتادة: نعم والله متظاهرة لقهرك بها كتما لشكر

THALABI:v10p209/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p209/r1.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v10p209/r1.claim: The Prophet says God provided two coverings each for the tongue, eyes, and private parts, so a person can shut them when they seek what is forbidden.
THALABI:v10p209/r1.anchor: عن أبي حازم قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ابن آدم إن نازعك لسانك فيما حرمت عليك فقد أعنتك عليه بطبقين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p21/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p21/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p21/r1.claim: The two eyes are among the signs enabling a person to recognize that God can resurrect him and reckon his deeds.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p21/r1.anchor: ألم نفعل به ما يستدل به على أن الله قادر

WAHIDI-QT:90:8/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:90:8/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:90:8/r1.claim: The eyes, tongue, and lips God gave him show that God can hold him to account for his deeds.
WAHIDI-QT:90:8/r1.anchor: ثم ذكر ما يستدل به على أن الله تعالى قادر عليه وأن يحصي عليه ما يعمله فقال { ألم نجعل له عينين } { ولسانا وشفتين }

WAHIDI-QT:90:9/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:90:9/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:90:9/r1.claim: The eyes, tongue, and lips God gave him show that God can hold him to account for his deeds.
WAHIDI-QT:90:9/r1.anchor: ثم ذكر ما يستدل به على أن الله تعالى قادر عليه وأن يحصي عليه ما يعمله فقال { ألم نجعل له عينين } { ولسانا وشفتين }

ELMALILI:90:8-10/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r1.claim: The two eyes may be the two visible eyes or one visible eye together with the heart's eye.
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r1.anchor: Bu iki gözden murad iki zâhir gözü olabileceği gibi biri zâhir gözü, biri kalb gözü olmak da muhtemildir.

ELMALILI:90:8-10/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r2.claim: Eyes let a person see what is visible, so their gift raises the reproachful question whether their creator does not also see the person's deeds.
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r2.anchor: o hâlde o yaptıklarını görüyor da onu ve o gözleri yaratan ve gözetip duran Allah görmez mi?

ELMALILI:90:8-10/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r5.claim: The rhetorical question is an affirmation whose sense is yes, We made them.
ELMALILI:90:8-10/r5.anchor: Bu istifham takrîrî olduğu için mânanın hâsılı نـَعَمْ جَعَلْنَا “evet yaptık” meâlindedir.

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:8-9:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:8-9:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:8-9:anmerkung/r1.claim: Lists of divine favors often use a question with ʾa-lam plus a verb; compare reminders of God's favors to the Messenger in 93:6–8 and 94:1–4.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:8-9:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Auflistungen göttlicher Wohltaten begegnen wie hier häufig in Frageform, ʾa-lam + Verb, „Haben wir nicht / hat er nicht …?“

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r1.claim: The second stanza resumes the human-being statement at the introduction’s end and consists of two triplets marked by rhyme; the repeated third-person polemical questions formally unify them.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r1.anchor: Das zweite Gesätz, das pronominal an den ʾinsān-Spruch am Ende des Einleitungsgesätzes anknüpft, gliedert sich in zwei reimlich voneinander abgesetzte Dreiergruppen

CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r5.claim: The second triplet lists God’s gifts of sight, speech, and moral direction, recalling the human being’s creation in 90:4; its rhyme shift accents the contrast with human self-importance.
CORPUSCORANICUM:90:5-10:kommentar/r5.anchor: Gottes Ausstattung des Menschen mit Sehsinn, Sprechwerkzeugen und moralischer Orientierung aufzählt und damit auf die bereits in V. 90:4 festgehaltene Geschaffenheit des Menschen zurückverweist

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r2.claim: The eyes given to the human directly answer his thought that nobody saw him.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p263/r2.anchor: ارتباط قوله تعالى: {أَلَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُ عَيْنَيْنِ} بقوله: {أَيَحْسَبُ أَن لَّمْ يَرَهُ أَحَدٌ}

ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#3/r1.claim: God gave him two eyes with which to see.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p136#3/r1.anchor: ألم نجعل له عينين يبصر بهما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r3.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r3.claim: Qatada says the eyes, tongue, and lips are conspicuous blessings that remind a person to give thanks.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: نعم الله متظاهرة يقررك بها كيما تشكر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r4.claim: A hadith presents God telling Adam’s child to close the lips when the tongue seeks the forbidden, shut the eyes when sight seeks it, and likewise restrain the sexual organ.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p431/r4.anchor: وجاء في الحديث: أن الله عز وجل يقول: ابن آدم إن نازعك لسانك فيما حرمت عليك

BAYDAWI-FULL:90:6-9/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:90:6-9/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:90:6-9/r3.claim: God gave him two eyes with which to see.
BAYDAWI-FULL:90:6-9/r3.anchor: ألم نجعل له عينين } يبصر بهما

BINTSHATI:v1p181/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p181/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p181/r1.claim: The eyes, tongue, and lips signify accountable use of sight and speech, not merely body parts shared with animals; this prepares the warning about moral responsibility and the consequences of words.
BINTSHATI:v1p181/r1.anchor: وإنما يراد بها ما يسأل الإنسان عنه، على وجه الحض والزجر بالحجة، من أمانة البصر والنطق

BINTSHATI:v1p182/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r4.claim: The sequence shows a human equipped with senses and innate discernment to bear the difficult trust of moral responsibility and choose between the clearly visible paths.
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r4.anchor: فهذا الإنسان الذي خلقه الله مهيأ لأمانة التكليف الصعبة

BINTSHATI:v1p182/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r5.claim: Past tense with alam suits senses granted before the arrogant person feels powerful, while lan projects forward his deluded claim that no one will ever overpower him.
BINTSHATI:v1p182/r5.anchor: أما حسبانه أن لن يقدر عليه أحد، فيأتي متأخراً بعد أن تطغيه القوة والمال

BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r2.claim: God gave two eyes for seeing and acting in the sensory world; their precise formation in the womb and power of sight exceed human understanding.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r2.anchor: شققناهما وهو في الرحم في ظلمات ثلاثة على مقدار مناسب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r3.claim: The eyes should prompt gratitude and use of perception in what God permits and avoidance of what He forbids.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p429/r3.anchor: مذكرا له بما كان يجب عليه من الشكر باستعمال هذه المشاعر

DURR-FULL:v8p521/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r5.claim: He takes the two eyes as one of further benefits, leaving the rest unspecified with ‘and so on.’
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r5.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله: {يقول أهلكت مالا لبدا} قال: أيمن علينا فما فضلناه أفضل {ألم نجعل له عينين} وكذا وكذا

DURR-FULL:v8p521/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r6.claim: The eyes are among God's abundant blessings, reminders intended to make people give thanks.
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r6.anchor: عن قتادة {ألم نجعل له عينين} قال: نعم من الله متظاهرة يقررنا بها كيما نشكر

DURR-FULL:v8p521/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r7.claim: A divine address calls the eyes and their lids great blessings, to look at what is lawful and close them against what is forbidden.
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r7.anchor: عن مكحول رضي الله عنه قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: يقول الله يا ابن آدم قد أنعمت عليك نعما عظاما

DURR-FULL:v8p521/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r10.claim: The address warns that a human cannot bear God's anger or withstand His vengeance.
DURR-FULL:v8p521/r10.anchor: ابن آدم إنك لا تحمل سخطي ولا تستطيع انتقامي

DAMGHANI:v1p338/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p338/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p338/r3.claim: ʿAynān means the two literal eyes.
DAMGHANI:v1p338/r3.anchor: الخامس العين الناظرة بعينها قوله سبحانه في سورة البلد

DAMGHANI:v1p338/r10.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p338/r10.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p338/r10.claim: The entry’s heading also lists elevation or riding over, drowsiness, and darkness among the senses of ghishiya, without examples in this excerpt.
DAMGHANI:v1p338/r10.anchor: الغشاوة الغطاء الغاشية القيامة الاخذ التراكب والتراكم العلو التغشية النعاس الظلمة

ABUHAYYAN:90:8/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:90:8/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:90:8/r1.claim: God enumerates blessings: eyes for seeing, a tongue for expressing what is within, and lips for closing the mouth and aiding eating, drinking, blowing, and more.
ABUHAYYAN:90:8/r1.anchor: ثم عدد تعالى على الإنسان نعمه فقال : { ألم نجعل له عينين } يبصر بهما ، { ولساناً } يفصح عما في باطنه ، { وشفتين } يطبقهما على فيه

ALUSI:90:7/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:90:7/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:90:7/r5.claim: The reminder of the two eyes follows to establish God’s power to requite and account for the person, as well as His knowledge of his state.
ALUSI:90:7/r5.anchor: وقرر سبحانه القدرة على مجازاته ومحاسبته والإطلاع على حاله

ALUSI:90:8/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:90:8/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:90:8/r1.claim: God made the person two eyes with which to see; in context this supports the reminder that God observes and can hold him to account.

BAGHAWI:90:8/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:90:8/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:90:8/r1.claim: God reminds the person of His favors so that he will reflect; He gave him eyes, a tongue, and lips.
BAGHAWI:90:8/r1.anchor: ثم ذكره نعمه ليعتبر فقال :{ ألم نجعل له عينين ولساناً وشفتين }

BAGHAWI:90:8/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:90:8/r2.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI:90:8/r2.claim: Qatada says God's successive favors confront and remind a person so that he will give thanks.
BAGHAWI:90:8/r2.anchor: قال قتادة : نعم الله متظاهرة يقررك بها كيما تشكر

BAGHAWI:90:8/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:90:8/r3.speaker: الحديث
BAGHAWI:90:8/r3.claim: A hadith reports God saying that He gave a person ways to restrain forbidden speech, sight, and sexual desire by closing the lips, eyes, and other bodily means.
BAGHAWI:90:8/r3.anchor: في الحديث : " أن الله عز وجل يقول : ابن آدم إن نازعك لسانك فيما حرمت عليك فقد أعنتك عليه بطبقتين فأطبق

BAYDAWI:90:8/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:90:8/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:90:8/r1.claim: The reminder that God gave the person two eyes clarifies the preceding warning about being seen.
BAYDAWI:90:8/r1.anchor: ثم بين ذلك بقوله ألم نجعل له عينين يبصر بهما

BIQAI:90:6/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:6/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:90:6/r5.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says that even though people possess eyes and other means of reflection, they fail to save themselves; he points to the challenge to climb the steep path.

BIQAI:90:8/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:8/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:90:8/r1.claim: The two eyes include physical sight of the sensory world and the inner eye's insight into the moral world, opening desires for perceived good and escape from perceived evil.
BIQAI:90:8/r1.anchor: نظر العين الباصرة الجائلة في العالم الحسي ونظر عين البصيرة

BIQAI:90:8/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:8/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:90:8/r2.claim: The reminder establishes that the benefactor knows all human affairs and can bring benefit or harm, personally or through whomever He wills.
BIQAI:90:8/r2.anchor: عالماً بجميع أمره قادراً على نفعه وضره بنفسه

BIQAI:90:8/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:90:8/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:90:8/r3.claim: Eyes are made in the womb within three darknesses, proportioned symmetrically and given varied colors; their sight works beyond creation's understanding. Their gift calls for grateful, lawful use.
BIQAI:90:8/r3.anchor: شققناهما وهو في الرحم في ظلمات ثلاث على مقدار مناسب لا يزيد إحداهما على الأخرى

DURR:90:8/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:90:8/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR:90:8/r1.claim: Qatada calls the two eyes one of God's repeated blessings, by which He reminds people so that they may give thanks.
DURR:90:8/r1.anchor: عن قتادة { ألم نجعل له عينين } قال : نعم من الله متظاهرة يقررنا بها كيما نشكر

DURR:90:8/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:90:8/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:90:8/r2.claim: The Prophet conveys God's reminder that people should use their eyes, speech, and sexual faculties only in lawful ways; they cannot bear God's anger or withstand His vengeance.
DURR:90:8/r2.anchor: عن مكحول رضي الله عنه قال : قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : «يقول الله يا ابن آدم قد أنعمت عليك نعماً عظاماً لا تحصي عدها

IBNATIYYA:90:8/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:90:8/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:90:8/r1.claim: God then enumerates the human's bodily faculties as blessings that establish the proof against him.
IBNATIYYA:90:8/r1.anchor: ثم عدد تعالى على الإنسان نعمه التي بها تقوم الحجة وهي جوارحه

IBNKATHIR:90:8/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:90:8/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:90:8/r1.claim: God made him two eyes with which to see.
IBNKATHIR:90:8/r1.anchor: وقوله : { أَلَمْ نَجْعَلْ لَهُ عَيْنَيْنِ } أي : يبصر بهما

KASHSHAF:90:8/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:90:8/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:90:8/r1.claim: God gave the human two eyes with which to see visible things.

NASAFI:90:8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:90:8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:90:8/r1.claim: God reminds the human of His favors, including two eyes with which to see visible things.
NASAFI:90:8/r1.anchor: { أَلَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُ عَيْنَيْنِ } يبصر بهما المرئيات

QURTUBI:90:8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:8/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:90:8/r1.claim: God enumerates His blessings: He gave the person eyes for seeing, a tongue for speech, and lips to cover the mouth; the One who did this can resurrect and reckon his deeds.
QURTUBI:90:8/r1.anchor: ثم عدد عليه نعمه فقال : " ألم نجعل له عينين " يبصر بهما " ولسانا " ينطق به

QURTUBI:90:8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:8/r2.speaker: أبو حازم
QURTUBI:90:8/r2.claim: Abu Hazim reports that the Prophet conveyed God's warning that people have been given lips to close against forbidden speech, eyelids against forbidden sight, and coverings against forbidden sexual desire.
QURTUBI:90:8/r2.anchor: وقال أبو حازم : قال النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم : ( إن اللّه تعالى قال : يا ابن آدم ، إن نازعك لسانك فيما حرمت عليك ، فقد أعنتك عليه بطبقين ، فأطبق

QURTUBI:90:8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:90:8/r6.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI:90:8/r6.claim: Qatada says God's blessings are evident, and that He reminds the person of them so that he will give thanks.
QURTUBI:90:8/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة : نعم اللّه ظاهرة ، يقررك بها حتى تشكر

RAZI:90:8/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:8/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:90:8/r1.claim: After reporting the disbeliever’s question about whether anyone sees him, God points to the creation of his eyes as evidence of divine power.
RAZI:90:8/r1.anchor: لما حكى عن ذلك الكافر قوله

RAZI:90:8/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:8/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:90:8/r2.claim: The extraordinary properties of bodily organs are discussed in books of anatomy.
RAZI:90:8/r2.anchor: وعجائب هذه الأعضاء مذكورة في كتب التشريح

RAZI:90:8/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:8/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:90:8/r3.claim: Najd is an elevated road; clear proofs are like a high road plainly visible to the eyes, and most exegetes take the two roads as good and evil.
RAZI:90:8/r3.anchor: النجد الطريق في ارتفاع فكأنه لما وضحت الدلائل

RAZI:90:8/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:8/r4.speaker: أبي هريرة
RAZI:90:8/r4.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet saying the two roads are the road of good and the road of evil, and that no one should prefer evil’s road.
RAZI:90:8/r4.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة أنه عليه السلام قال : «إنما هما النجدان

RAZI:90:8/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:8/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:90:8/r5.claim: The verse parallels the passage on human creation with hearing and sight and guidance to the two paths, whether grateful or ungrateful.
RAZI:90:8/r5.anchor: وهذه الآية كالآية في : { هل أتى على الإنسان }

RAZI:90:8/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:8/r6.speaker: الحسن
RAZI:90:8/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the boast asks who will hold the spender accountable; the answer is the One who created his organs.
RAZI:90:8/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن : قال { أهلكت مالا لبدا }

RAZI:90:8/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:8/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن المسيب
RAZI:90:8/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib interpret the two elevated paths as the two breasts, paths of a child’s life and provision.
RAZI:90:8/r7.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس وسعيد بن المسيب ،   أنهما الثديان

RAZI:90:8/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:8/r8.speaker: القفال
RAZI:90:8/r8.claim: Al-Qaffāl prefers the interpretation that the two paths are the paths of good and evil.

RAZI:90:8/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:90:8/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:90:8/r9.claim: The One who made a rational heart and eloquent tongue from humble fluid can destroy what He created and knows what creatures conceal; denying God and spending against His religion have no excuse.
RAZI:90:8/r9.anchor: إن من قدر على أن يخلق من الماء المهين قلبا عقولا
